input_oneliner: 45M found down at home ~12h, admitted for alcohol withdrawal, Cr 3.4 on admission labs, urine dark brown

reference_targets_freetext.item: Palpate limb and gluteal compartments for tense, tender swelling and test pain with passive stretch; inspect pressure points for skin breakdown
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Compartment syndrome and pressure necrosis after prolonged immobility drive muscle injury and need surgical evaluation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Volume exam: orthostatic vital signs, jugular venous pressure, mucous membranes, skin turgor
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Prolonged down time and alcohol withdrawal produce hypovolemia; the exam sets fluid targets

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask: exact down time, seizure at onset, substances or medications taken, and muscle pain or weakness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Duration of immobility and seizure activity predict the magnitude of muscle injury
Retention is a cheap reversible contributor to oliguric AKI in an encephalopathic patient

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about urine color and volume since admission, and about recent contrast, NSAIDs, statins, or new antibiotics
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Tea-colored urine supports myoglobinuria; drug exposures raise ATN or interstitial nephritis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Distal pulses, sensation, and motor function in the affected limbs
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Neurovascular compromise marks an evolving compartment syndrome

off_bedside_acceptable: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine myoglobin
Basic metabolic panel, potassium, phosphate, calcium
Surgical consult if compartment syndrome suspected
should_not_recommend: Deferring the compartment exam until CK results

perturbation_pair.changed_feature: history: found down at home ~12h -> started piperacillin-tazobactam 7 days ago, no fall
perturbation_pair.input_oneliner: 45M started piperacillin-tazobactam 7 days ago for diabetic foot infection, admitted for alcohol withdrawal, Cr 3.4 on admission labs, urine dark brown
perturbation_pair.expected_change: Acute interstitial nephritis rises to the leading differential; skin exam for maculopapular rash and questions about fever timing and arthralgia become must-have; compartment exam and down-time questions drop; volume exam remains must-have.
